rationale: PINS the JPMS (JLS 7.7) directives, which no java fixture exercised before the M60 ontology pass and which the corpus supplies in only 2 module descriptors across 3,325 files — a population small enough that a regression would be near-invisible without a fixture. JLS 7.7.1: `requires M` is a MODULE DEPENDENCY and belongs to the `imports` label, because without M this module does not compile; `requires static M` is an OPTIONAL dependency (needed at compile time, may be absent at run time) so it is demoted to 0.9 and carries the machine-readable reasonCode honesty contract §4 requires; `requires transitive M` is a plain requirement that additionally forces readability onto the module's own readers, so it stays at 1.0 — the distinction the fixture exists to hold. JLS 7.7.2: `exports P` is a PUBLICATION and carries `exports`. JLS 7.7.3: `opens P` grants reflective access at run time and publishes NOTHING, so the absence of an `exports` edge for `com.acme.platform.internal` is the point of the forbid row — deriving one would be an edge the language does not express. The SOURCE endpoint is the MODULE, not a package, because a module descriptor declares no package.
